presentingComplaint: 24-year-old man with known homozygous sickle cell disease (HbSS) presents with severe generalized bone and joint pain of 8 hours' duration, rated 9/10, involving the lower back, bilateral thighs, and long bones, similar in character to his prior crises but more severe.
history: Known HbSS since infancy, on hydroxyurea (reports inconsistent adherence over the past month) with baseline hemoglobin 8.0-8.5 g/dL. Approximately 8 crises requiring hospitalization in the past 3 years, none requiring exchange transfusion or ICU care. No history of acute chest syndrome, stroke, or priapism. Pain began abruptly this morning after a day of outdoor manual labor in hot weather with reduced fluid intake; no preceding trauma. Denies fever, cough, chest pain, or dyspnea at onset. No recent travel, no sick contacts, no diarrhea. Not on chronic opioids at baseline; uses NSAIDs and oral hydration for mild crises at home, which have not controlled this episode. No history of transfusion in the past 3 months (low alloimmunization/delayed hemolytic transfusion reaction risk for this episode). Vaccinated per sickle cell protocol (pneumococcal, meningococcal, Hib) per history.
examination: Alert, in obvious distress from pain, grimacing, guarding lower extremities and back, unable to find a comfortable position. No pallor out of proportion to baseline. Mild scleral icterus (chronic hemolysis). No focal bony tenderness suggesting fracture; diffuse tenderness over lumbar spine, femora, and tibiae bilaterally without swelling, erythema, or warmth of joints. Chest clear to auscultation, no crepitations, no splinting. Abdomen soft, mild non-focal tenderness, no rebound, spleen not palpable (prior autosplenectomy likely). No priapism. No focal neurological deficit. No calf tenderness or asymmetric limb swelling.
imaging: Chest X-ray: no infiltrate, no consolidation, normal cardiac silhouette
Plain films of painful long bones: no fracture, no periosteal reaction
microbiology: Blood cultures pending (drawn given mild leukocytosis, not yet resulted)

finalDiagnosis: Sickle cell vaso-occlusive crisis (severe pain crisis), uncomplicated by acute chest syndrome or sepsis

contraindications: Avoid NSAIDs if renal impairment or concurrent sickle nephropathy

Avoid routine antibiotics without evidence of infection (no source identified here)
edgeCases: If fever, hypoxia, or new infiltrate develop, reclassify as acute chest syndrome - a distinct, more urgent diagnosis
